title: Room and Harvest
premise: Ines Sandoval takes a teaching post in the fading town of Marrow Bend, where students vanish one by one and the town treats the disappearances as weather. The horror centers on his grandmother's house, where old photographs keep gaining an extra empty chair, marking a seat reserved for something invited in generations ago. As the harvest moon approaches, Ines uncovers that the town's founding families made a covenant trading their children for prosperity, and that his own bloodline holds the deciding vote. In the climax he refuses to fill the chair with another child, offering himself instead; surviving until sunrise breaks the covenant but leaves him changed, half-remembered by everyone who knew him.
about_author: Odile Crane is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in towns too small to appear on maps. She writes horror about institutions, inheritance, and the quiet violence of belonging.

chapters.title: The Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Ines arrives in Marrow Bend and moves into his late grandmother's house. POV: Ines. He counts eleven doors at night and twelve by morning, dismissing it as grief. Emotional beat: uneasy new beginnings.

chapters.title: Attendance Is Sacred
chapters.summary: First day teaching seventh grade; Principal Voss insists attendance is 'a covenant matter.' A student, Denny Ruiz, mentions his sister 'went to the farm.' POV: Ines. Beat: wrongness beneath routine.

chapters.title: Photographs of Grandmother's Parlor
chapters.summary: Ines sorts family photos and finds an extra wooden chair in every image after 1962, always empty, never commented on. POV: Ines. Beat: creeping dread disguised as nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Three students absent in one week; their desks are removed overnight without paperwork. Ines asks questions and receives identical, rehearsed answers. POV: Ines. Beat: institutional gaslighting.

chapters.title: Denny Knows the Rules
chapters.summary: Denny warns Ines never to set a thirteenth place at dinner and never answer a knock after the porch light dies. POV: Ines. Beat: a child's fatalism chilling the adult.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines finds a leather ledger in the school archive listing names paired with years of 'good yield.' His grandmother's name appears twice. POV: Ines. Beat: curiosity curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Chair Moves Closer
chapters.summary: In photographs taken this week, the extra chair now sits nearer the camera each day. Ines burns one photo; the ash smells like bread. POV: Ines. Beat: the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: Sheriff Aldous Pays a Visit
chapters.summary: The sheriff checks on the 'new teacher,' asking whether Ines has been invited anywhere yet. He leaves a jar of honey from the Hollis farm. POV: Ines. Beat: hospitality as threat.

chapters.title: Marta Hollis's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ines visits the Hollis farm where missing students supposedly go; Marta feeds him pie and describes her own daughter as 'harvested well.' POV: Ines. Beat: sweetness hiding rot.

chapters.title: What Grandma Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: Repairing a plaster crack, Ines finds a tin box: a covenant deed signed by founding families, including a Sandoval. POV: Ines. Beat: inheritance as sentence.

chapters.title: Denny Doesn't Come to School
chapters.summary: Denny vanishes; his desk disappears before lunch. Ines confronts Voss and is suspended for 'disrupting the season.' POV: Ines. Beat: grief weaponized into isolation.

chapters.title: Twelve Doors, Locked
chapters.summary: Night at grandma's house: all doors lock themselves, and footsteps pace the twelfth room Ines cannot find. POV: Ines. Beat: the house turning hostile.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Ines canvasses neighbors; every adult gives the same smile and the same phrase: 'It keeps us fed.' POV: Ines. Beat: loneliness of seeing clearly.

chapters.title: A Voice Through the Wall
chapters.summary: Something in the walls speaks in Denny's voice, asking to be let into the warm rooms. Ines nearly opens the door. POV: Ines. Beat: compassion as trap.

chapters.title: Reverend Pike's Confession Fragment
chapters.summary: The dying reverend tells Ines the covenant requires a Sandoval to seat the guest or unseat it, then dies mid-sentence. POV: Ines. Beat: hope arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Photographs Complete
chapters.summary: Every photo now shows the chair pulled up to the table, and a faint figure seated in the oldest ones. POV: Ines. Beat: the invitation nearing acceptance.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Trade
chapters.summary: Voss reveals the school exists to select the harvest and offers to spare Ines if he nominates a student. POV: Ines. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ines Refuses, Badly
chapters.summary: Ines publicly accuses Voss at a town meeting; the town turns on him with serene unanimity. POV: Ines. Beat: justice failing inside the law.

chapters.title: Ally in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Ruthie, a teenage survivor hidden in the Hollis orchard, contacts Ines; she escaped the harvest two years ago and remembers everything. POV: Ruthie. Beat: solidarity kindling.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Saw
chapters.summary: Ruthie describes the harvest night: the guest wears the faces of the missing, seated at a table that isn't there by daylight. POV: Ruthie. Beat: witness as burden.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Grandma
chapters.summary: Ines dreams of his grandmother performing a rite at the table, whispering 'not yet, not mine.' He wakes with flour on his hands. POV: Ines. Beat: ancestral love revealed as resistance.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Archive
chapters.summary: Ines and Ruthie steal the full ledger from the school, learning the covenant renews each harvest moon unless the deciding bloodline seats itself. POV: alternating. Beat: plan forming against the clock.

chapters.title: Three Days to the Moon
chapters.summary: Preparations: salt lines fail, mirrors fog with breath not theirs. The town watches them with pity. POV: Ines. Beat: dread arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Honey Turns
chapters.summary: Everyone who ate Sheriff Aldous's honey begins sleepwalking toward the Hollis farm at night, including half Ines's class. POV: Ines. Beat: the whole town complicit in its body.

chapters.title: Ruthie Taken
chapters.summary: Ruthie is lured out by her mother's voice and vanishes; only her shoes remain in the orchard. POV: Ines. Beat: guilt and fury.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Door Opens
chapters.summary: Ines finally finds the twelfth door behind grandma's pantry mirror: a stair down to a parlor identical to the one upstairs. POV: Ines. Beat: threshold crossed.

chapters.title: The Table Below
chapters.summary: Beneath the house stands the long table from the photographs, thirteen chairs, twelve occupied by the missing, faces intact, eyes vacant. POV: Ines. Beat: horror of the kept-alive.

chapters.title: Denny at the Table
chapters.summary: Ines reaches Denny, who can speak only in menu-words: 'supper,' 'guest,' 'seat.' The thing in the head chair turns to look at him. POV: Ines. Beat: heartbreak sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Covenant Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ines reads the deed at the table; the terms confirm a Sandoval may substitute himself for the harvest, once, forever. POV: Ines. Beat: the terrible clarity of choice.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Voss arrives to complete the ritual, revealing she was harvested long ago and returned as steward. POV: Voss flashback within Ines's scene. Beat: villain as victim.

chapters.title: Moonrise
chapters.summary: The harvest moon rises; the house above groans and rearranges; the guest begins to stand. POV: Ines. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Ines Takes the Chair
chapters.summary: Ines sits in the thirteenth chair and declares himself the invited guest, severing the town's debt. The vacant faces turn toward freedom. POV: Ines. Beat: sacrifice as defiance.

chapters.title: Holding Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: Seated, Ines endures the guest wearing his memories, his mother's voice, his own face, bargaining for him to leave the chair. POV: Ines. Beat: identity under siege.

chapters.title: The Longest Hour
chapters.summary: Ruthie, released when the covenant broke, descends and anchors Ines with his real name and real stories the guest gets wrong. POV: Ruthie. Beat: being known as salvation.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Light enters the below-parlor; the guest unravels into grain dust; the twelve wake, hollow but alive. POV: Ines. Beat: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: The Town Forgets Him
chapters.summary: The price: those saved remember nothing of Ines except a vague kindness; records of him fade. Only Ruthie, outside the covenant, remembers fully. POV: Ruthie. Beat: bittersweet erasure.

chapters.title: Twelve Doors Again
chapters.summary: Ines walks the house at dawn counting doors: twelve, all his, none locked. The extra chair sits by the window, empty, harmless. POV: Ines. Beat: peace earned.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ines and Ruthie burn the ledgers and the deed; Voss crumbles to dust with the covenant. No court, no confession—just ash and open windows. POV: alternating. Beat: reckoning without ceremony.

chapters.title: A New Attendance Sheet
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the school reopens under a temporary teacher; Denny raises his hand in class, remembering nothing but feeling safe. POV: Denny. Beat: ordinary life restored.

chapters.title: Room and Harvest
chapters.summary: Ines leaves Marrow Bend at dusk, Ruthie driving. In the rearview, the house lights go dark room by room, politely, like someone saying goodnight. POV: Ines. Beat: departure, belonging carried rather than found.
